difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a locally Noetherian integral scheme X and a nonzero rational function f, the prime divisors whose generic point does not contain f in its local ring, and those with nonzero order at f, form locally finite collections (source lines 6630-6643). The proof finds a nonempty open U over which f is a unit, so every prime divisor occurring in either collection is an irreducible component of the complement of U, and invokes local finiteness of the components of a closed subset.
